source_note: Study-aid summaries authored during the hub build (Phase 4). Standard titles are the official titles; summaries are study aids, NOT the standard text. Verify all detail against the official standard before relying on it. No paragraph numbers are cited anywhere in this module, by policy.

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Sets the overall requirements for presenting financial statements: a complete set (SFP, SOPL/OCI, changes in equity, cash flows, notes), going-concern basis, accrual basis, materiality and aggregation, no offsetting unless permitted, comparative information, and consistency of presentation.
standards.title: Presentation of Financial Statements

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost includes purchase costs, conversion costs and other costs to bring inventories to their present location and condition. Abnormal waste, storage (unless necessary) and selling costs are excluded from cost.
standards.title: Inventories

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Requires the statement of cash flows classifying flows into operating, investing and financing activities, using either the direct or indirect method for operating cash flows.
standards.title: Statement of Cash Flows

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Current tax is the tax payable on taxable profit. Deferred tax is recognised on temporary differences between carrying amounts and tax bases: deferred tax liabilities for taxable temporary differences, deferred tax assets for deductible ones (only when probable future taxable profit exists). Deferred tax is not discounted.
standards.title: Income Taxes

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: PPE is recognised when future economic benefits are probable and cost is reliably measurable. Cost model: carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment. Each significant part is depreciated separately over its useful life; residual values and useful lives are reviewed annually.
standards.title: Property, Plant and Equipment

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Covers short-term benefits, post-employment benefits (defined contribution vs defined benefit plans), other long-term benefits and termination benefits. Defined benefit obligations are measured using the projected unit credit method.
standards.title: Employee Benefits

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: An asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount (the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use). Goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles are tested annually regardless of indicators.
standards.title: Impairment of Assets

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: A provision is recognised only when there is a present obligation from a past event, an outflow of resources is probable, and a reliable estimate can be made. Contingent liabilities are disclosed, not recognised; contingent assets are disclosed only when inflow is probable.
standards.title: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

standards.source_note: Title per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Intangible assets are recognised when probable future benefits and reliably measurable cost exist. Research is expensed; development is capitalised only when strict criteria are met. Finite-life intangibles are amortised; indefinite-life intangibles are tested for impairment annually.
standards.title: Intangible Assets

standards.source_note: Title and effective date per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Financial assets are classified by the business-model test and the SPPI test into amortised cost, fair value through OCI, or fair value through profit or loss. Introduces the expected credit loss impairment model.
standards.title: Financial Instruments

standards.source_note: Title and effective date per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Sets the fair value hierarchy (Levels 1-3) and disclosure requirements.
standards.title: Fair Value Measurement

standards.source_note: Title and effective date per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Revenue from contracts with customers follows five steps: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied (control transferred).
standards.title: Revenue from Contracts with Customers

standards.source_note: Title and effective date per official standard; summary is a study aid.
standards.summary: Lessees recognise a right-of-use asset and lease liability for almost all leases (exemptions: short-term and low-value). The liability is the present value of lease payments; the asset is depreciated and the liability accrues interest.
standards.title: Leases
